la:noun:Messalla.html:
Messalla (less correctly Messāla), ae, m.,
a Roman surname in the gens Valeria: Corvinus primus Messanam vicit, et pri mus ex familiā Valeriorum, urbis captae in se translato nomine, Messana appellatus est: paulatimque vulgo permutante litteras, Messalla dictus,. The most celebrated is the orator M. Valerius Messalla Corvinus, in the time of Cicero and Augustus, ; , A, 5; ; ; .—In plur., .

la:noun:messis.html:
messis, is (
acc. sing. messim, ; ; ; ; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 200), f. (masc.: non magno messe, Lucil. ap. ) [id.], a reaping and ingathering of the fruits of the earth, a harvest (class.).
Lit.: messis proprio nomine dicitur in iis, quae metuntur, maxime in frumento,; ; ; ; : seges matura messi,: messem hordaceam facere, aream in messem creta praeparare,to get in the harvest,: messe amissā,: messis feria, Cod. 3, 10, 2.—Of the gathering of honey,.—
Transf., concr., harvest.
The harvested crops, the harvest: illius immensae ruperunt horrea messes,; ; ; : Cilicum et Arabum, the harvest of the Arabians, i. e. saffron and frankincense, : bellatura,the men that sprang from the dragon's teeth sown by Cadmus,. —
The crops that are to be harvested, the standing crops, the harvest: messium incensores, vel vinearum olivarumve,: messes suas urere, prov., like vineta sua caedere, i. e. to destroy one's own work (e. g. one's own pupils), : adhuc tua messis in herba est, your wheat is still in the blade, i. e. you are premature in your expectations, .—
The time of harvest, harvest-time: si frigus erit, si messis,.—Poet. transf. for a year: sexagesima messis,. —
Trop.: pro benefactis mali messem metere,to receive evil for good, to reap ingratitude,: uberem messem mali,: (morum malorum) metere messem maxumam,: si attigeris ostium, jam tibi hercle in ore fiet messis mergis pugneis,: Sullani temporis messem, the harvest of the time of Sylla, when so many were killed, ; (in eccl. Lat.) the time for winning souls to the truth: transiit messis, finita est aestas, et nos salvati non sumus,.—Of the persons to be gathered into the church: messis quidem multa,; cf. . —Of the end of the world: sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem,; cf. v. 39.
